subject: Pilot criteria & cost constraints for Ledgerly inference
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Claire Harper <claire@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Ledgerly discovery - unit economics, batching + quantization openness

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap to make sure we captured Ledgerly's priorities and to propose next steps. Please correct anything I got wrong.

High-level pain points you shared
- Token cost pressure on user-facing features (invoice summarization + Q&A) as volume scales 3x over the next 12 months
- Latency requirement: 95th percentile end-to-end < 350ms for short queries (~50 tokens)
- Ops friction: current in-house endpoints are brittle and scaling costs spike unpredictably during batch jobs

Current stack
- Inference: internal endpoints on g4dn-family VMs, running an Llama-variant, CPU fallback for low-priority jobs
- Orchestration: homegrown autoscaler + SQS for batch jobs
- Monitoring: Datadog for infra metrics, limited token-level cost visibility

Success criteria for a pilot (what will make this a win for Ledgerly)
1) Per-token unit cost reduced by >= 30% for production traffic mix (defined by attached sample-traffic-profile.csv)
2) Maintained P95 latency < 350ms for real-time routes under production-like traffic
3) Seamless canary and rollback behavior for model updates during the pilot

Key signals we should measure in pilot
- Effective batching rates and latency distribution per route
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV) for repeated queries and corresponding cost delta
- Quality delta when trying 4-bit quantized model variant (prompt/response length-sensitive regression tests)

Openness to quantization
- You indicated Ledgerly is open to trying aggressive quantization (4-bit) for lower-criticality routes, but want to run automated evaluation against your prompt set first. Noted.

Proposed next steps
- We’ll prepare a lightweight pilot charter (attached) that defines traffic slices, evaluation prompts, and rollback policy — aim to get this signed in ~1 week
- Can you share a 24–72 hour sample of production traffic (anonymized) and target monthly token volume? The sample-traffic-profile.csv template is attached.
- I’ll loop in Aditya (SE) for a short technical call to align on batching, prefix caching, and quantization gating — can you do 30 minutes on Thursday?
- Procurement contact: please share the right procurement address to route the pilot SOW and SOC2 extracts.

Attachments: pilot charter + traffic template + SOC2 extracts stub.

If this looks right I’ll send the charter and a proposed calendar invite for the tech call.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Redwood Inference — production-grade LLM inference for engineering teams
From: Claire Harper <claire@ledgerly.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 16:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Ledgerly discovery - unit economics, batching + quantization openness

Soojin —

This looks good and captures our concerns well. Quick answers:
- We can share a 48-hour anonymized sample export by EOD Wednesday.
- Target monthly token volume for Q4 planning: ~1.8B tokens (mostly short replies, ~60% < 100 tokens)
- Procurement contact: procurement@ledgerly.com (I've CC'd them on this reply)
- Thursday 11:00am PT works for a 30m technical sync with Aditya.

Regarding quantization: yes, happy to trial 4-bit on less-critical routes (batch notifications, scheduled summarization). We want to see automated regression metrics against canonical prompts before expanding.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Harper
Head of AI Products, Ledgerly
claire@ledgerly.com | +1 (650) 555-3344

Great — thanks for the quick responses and for CC'ing procurement. Next actions below and owners:

1) Pilot charter + SOW (owner: Soojin) — I attached the pilot charter PDF (redwood-pilot-charter.pdf). Will push an editable Drive link once procurement confirms. Target: circulate for signature by next Tuesday.

2) Traffic sample (owner: Claire) — Claire to share the 48-hour anonymized sample (use the attached CSV template). We'll run a lightweight cost model against it to project per-token savings across batching and cache heuristics.

3) Technical sync (owner: Aditya) — 30m Thursday 11:00am PT to align on endpoints, max sequence lengths, and caching gates. Aditya will prepare a short checklist: supported batching window, expected KV cache hit rates, safe quantization fallbacks.

4) Regression criteria (owner: Ledgerly + Redwood) — define pass/fail thresholds for automated evaluation on the prompt set (we recommend: <=1.5% top-line delta on ROUGE-like metrics for extractive Q&A; subjective fallbacks for hallucination spikes).

Procurement: if you need a template SOW or references for SOC2 artifacts, I attached a SOC2 extracts zip and a one-page SOW checklist.

I’ll send calendar invites for the technical sync and a follow-up to confirm the charter circulation timeline.

Thanks — looking forward to getting a pilot scoped.

Soojin
On behalf of Redwood Inference
